record.original_question: Let S ⊂ P^3 be a very general quartic surface. If f: S → X is a dominant map of degree at least 2, what can be said about X? In particular, does the rationality conclusion known in degree d ≥ 5 continue to hold when d = 4?

evidence.quote: (13.1) We ask what happens for d = 4. (Easy step: pg(X) = q(X) = 0 and the fundamental group of X is trivial).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work over the complex numbers. Let $S \subset \mathbb{P}^3$ be a very general smooth quartic surface (so $S$ is a projective K3 surface with Picard rank one). Suppose $f : S \dashrightarrow X$ is a dominant rational map onto a smooth projective surface $X$ with $\deg f \geq 2$.

It is known that for a very general smooth surface $S_d \subset \mathbb{P}^3$ of degree $d \geq 5$, any such target $X$ must be rational. The question is whether the analogous conclusion holds for $d = 4$:

(a) Determine the possible birational types of the image $X$. In particular, must $X$ be a rational surface?

(b) As partial information, verify that any such $X$ satisfies $p_g(X) = q(X) = 0$ and $\pi_1(X) = 1$, and decide whether these constraints force $X$ to be rational.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this specific question for the quartic case (d=4) was located. Related work by Bastianelli and collaborators addresses dominant rational maps and measures of irrationality for surfaces in P^3 of degree d ≥ 5, but the d = 4 case appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On dominant rational maps from products of curves to surfaces of general type
status_evidence.snippet: Studies dominant rational maps from products of curves to surfaces of general type, related framework to the quartic surface question.
status_evidence.claim: Related literature treats dominant rational maps from/to surfaces but does not resolve the d=4 quartic case.

status_evidence.title: Rational maps from products of curves to surfaces with pg = q = 0
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses surfaces with vanishing geometric genus and irregularity arising as targets of dominant rational maps.
status_evidence.claim: Provides context on the constraints pg(X)=q(X)=0 mentioned in the problem.
